$comment: Parity fixture for the history-based duration lookup. Python: rhylthyme_server.rhylthyme.predict / rhylthyme_cli_runner.history.predict (tests/test_predict.py). JavaScript: predictDurations in rhylthyme-server/mcp-api/history.js (mcp-api/history.test.js, which reads this file by relative path). Each case carries the program (inline, or "thanksgiving" for rhylthyme-server/static/examples/thanksgiving_one_oven.json), the records (inline, or recordsFixture naming a sibling file), the prediction context in the JavaScript option spelling, and the full expected result keyed by stepId. expectApprox states what the generating law says, independently of either implementation.

cases.name: identical context
cases.comment: Five runs of the same version, environment and factor answers: the median is the prediction and P10/P90 the interval, no model needed.

cases.name: the caller's own identical runs win
cases.comment: Three of this cook's runs and four of everyone else's, all in the identical context. PRD open question 3: this cook's kitchen is the more relevant distribution, so source is "user" and n is 3.

cases.name: without a userId the same history pools every cook
cases.comment: The same records, asked without a userId: source "all", n 7.

cases.name: small n falls back to the median
cases.comment: Four measurements, none in the identical context (a different batch weight each time) and fewer than minModel: basis stays "model" but the method is the median and no factor is claimed.

cases.name: enum factors enter the model one-hot
cases.comment: Twelve runs where only the oven type matters (gas 1200 s, electric 1800 s, convection 900 s, +/- a little). batchKg is constant and so correlates with nothing; the surviving factors are one-hot oven columns and the prediction for a gas oven is 1200 s give or take the drift.

cases.name: an executor-controlled step is never predicted
cases.comment: The inferentiality report's verdict overrides the history: the measurements exist (n is reported) but the person, not the process, decides how long the step takes.

cases.name: no history
cases.comment: Runs of another program, an abandoned run and a time-scaled run: nothing usable, so no step gets an entry at all.

cases.name: video timelines are not history
cases.comment: One wall-clock run (1500 s) beside three video timeline records of the same program, version, environment and factors (runtime kind video, clockMode media): a dataset label, a person marking while watching, and one whose step even says executor. The clock rule drops all three, so the prediction is the wall run alone (n 1); counting all four would give n 4 and a median of 390 s.

cases.name: model fitted on the Thanksgiving corpus
cases.comment: Twenty synthetic runs whose turkey-roast obeys 600 + 90 * turkeyKg seconds. Asked for a 7 kg turkey in an electric oven — a combination the history has never seen — nothing is identical, so the lookup falls through to the model, keeps turkeyKg, drops the two one-hot oven columns (they correlate with nothing) and lands within 5% of the law's 1230 s. potatoes-boil obeys no law at all, so no factor survives and it comes back as the median of its measurements.

cases.name: identical beats the model on the same corpus
cases.comment: The same twenty runs asked for 7 kg in a gas oven: three runs match that context exactly, which is minIdentical, so the median of those three answers and the model is never fitted.

cases.name: this cook's own identical runs on the same corpus
cases.comment: All three runs in that identical context happen to be cook-1's own, so asking as cook-1 reports the same numbers with source "user": this kitchen's distribution, not 20 kitchens'.
